messages.summary: Shipper submits claim for PRO BLF-77209115 for a shipment that arrived May 12 (after the May 8 delivery date) with 2 cartons missing and 5 cartons crushed/wet; demands $29,920.00 covering shortage/damage, inspection/rework, the promotion markdown, and a freight refund.
Carrier requests the signed BOL, invoice, POD, damage photos, and inspection report, and asks that cargo loss be quantified separately from late-delivery business impact.

Shipper sends BOL, invoice, POD, and two photos; invoice shows 240 units at $425 each, POD shows 2 cartons short and 5 damaged (4 units/carton); direct shortage/damage subtotal is $9,350.00, pending the inspection write-up.

Carrier says only two photos were received and they don't cover all five damaged cartons, requests the inspection report and packaging specification, and flags a discrepancy between the EDI's 59 pieces delivered and the POD's 58 cartons received.

Shipper sends the inspection report showing 20 units from 5 cartons (14 unsellable, 6 repackable) with internal foam present; states the packaging specification is not in the claim folder; and raises an $18,000 markdown claim tied to MetroMart's May 10 promotion launch.

Carrier asserts the service was Standard LTL excluding consequential/loss-of-market delay damages, accepts 8 missing units and 9 of 14 damaged units (disputing the remaining 5), and offers $7,225.00 excluding inspection/repack expense, markdown, and freight refund.

Shipper disputes exclusion of the 5 units, citing the POD, inspection report, and foam presence, and asks carrier to reconsider the cargo amount, inspection/repack costs, and delay impact as a commercial compromise.
